summary: Adds two admin routes. DELETE /admin/users/:id removes one user, and POST /admin/users/purge removes a list of users by id.

findings.title: Delete user route lacks admin check
findings.problem: The DELETE /users/:id route omits the requireAdmin middleware. Both sibling routes in this router apply requireAdmin, and src/server.js adds no router-level guard.
findings.consequence: Any caller who reaches the server can delete any user by id. This includes callers with no session.
findings.fix: Add requireAdmin to the DELETE route, as the sibling routes do.

findings.title: Purge deletions float outside the handler
findings.problem: The purge handler passes an async callback to forEach, so nothing awaits or catches the db.removeUser promises. db.removeUser throws for an unknown id, and that rejection goes unhandled.
findings.consequence: One unknown id in a purge request raises an unhandled rejection, and Node then crashes the server. The response also reports every id as removed before any deletion finishes or fails.
findings.fix: Await the deletions with Promise.allSettled before responding. Report the count of fulfilled deletions.
findings.suggested_change:
const results = await Promise.allSettled(ids.map((id) => db.removeUser(id)));
  res.json({ removed: results.filter((r) => r.status === "fulfilled").length });

findings.title: New delete routes have no tests
findings.problem: This change adds the delete and purge routes, and the repository has no test that calls them.
findings.consequence: Without tests, the missing auth and the crash on an unknown id went unnoticed. Future regressions in these routes will go unnoticed too.
findings.fix: Add tests that cover auth, an unknown id and a mixed purge list for both routes.
